extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX users who need to typeset graphs and diagrams (mathematicians, computer scientists, and other technical authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Xy-pic TeX package to create graphs, commutative diagrams, knots, and other structured diagrams by leveraging its kernel, modules (options), and notation modes. Emphasises feature choices, backends, and resources for producing high-quality diagrams that match TeX typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel-and-options modular structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is structured as a kernel and several orthogonal modules called options, each defining a custom notation for a particular kind of graphical object or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These combinable logical composition structures let users mix notations appropriate to different graphical needs; choose and combine options to match the diagram semantics you want to express.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph combinator mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph combinator mode where diagrams are specified the way they are composed as graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this mode when you want to define diagrams by their graph composition rather than by matrix alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix-like (diagram) mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix-like mode where the dimensions of the drawing are computed by aligning diagram entries in rows and columns (this is the diagram mode Xy-pic version 2 users are used to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer this mode for traditional commutative diagrams and layouts that fit naturally into a grid of entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygon mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A polygon mode where diagrams shaped as regular polygons are entered in a simple way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when diagrams have a regular polygon arrangement; simplifies specifying evenly spaced vertices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knot-and-link typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: A mode for typesetting beautiful knots and links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specialized drawing primitives suitable for topology/knot diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turtle-graphics object-oriented mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A general object-oriented turtle graphic drawing language for specifying graphs with objects and connections between them in a manner independent of orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for procedural or programmatic construction of diagrams where orientation-independent placement is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible position specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions can be given in variety of formats (extendable) including user defined coordinates (x,y) and relative to previous positions, objects, object edges, and points on connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose absolute coordinates, relative positions, or references to other objects/edges depending on the layout control you need; extensible to user-defined formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object shapes and adjustability
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects may be circular, elliptic, or rectangular (more shapes can be added) and adjusted in several ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select shape and adjust sizing/appearance to match the visual semantics of diagram nodes; custom shapes can be added if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large library of mnemonic objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Large library of objects with mnemonic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuse built-in mnemonic-named objects where possible for clarity and consistency; refer to the reference manual for available objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects orienting along connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects that orient themselves along a connection when placed relative to it, e.g., @{|-} is like \vdash but thus oriented; new such objects can be defined in a convenient way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orientation-aware objects for arrows/labels that should follow path direction; define new oriented objects where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX boxes as objects
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX boxes, i.e., text and mathematical formulae, can be used as objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed text/math directly as node content to ensure consistent TeX typesetting within diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc primitives (circle segments and general arcs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes circle segments and optionally arbitrary elliptical, quadratic, and cubic arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these primitives for smooth curved connections or decorative elements; some arc types may depend on backend support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connections alignment and edge anchoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections are aligned between the reference points of objects but start and end on the edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect connections to line up logically between reference points while visually meeting object boundaries; adjust reference points or anchors to fine-tune endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any-object connections / diagonal filling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any object can be used to build a connection (using diagonal filling); library objects provide common line types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct custom connection appearances by composing objects; rely on library line types for standard styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible arrow and path notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexible notation for drawing arrows and general paths with tail, stem, and head built from any object(s). Special support for arrows that cross each other, arrows that go by other entries, paired arrows (including support for 2-cells), curved arrows, and arrows with bends. The style of arrow tips can be configured to match several styles of symbol arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose arrow parts from objects for highly customized arrowheads/tails; use built-in features for crossings, bypassing entries, paired arrows, and 2-cell notation in category-theory diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frames and braces library
rubrics_metrics.description: Library of frames and braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these frame/brace objects to group or annotate parts of diagrams visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations: rotation, scaling, colour, thickness
rubrics_metrics.description: Special notation for rotation, scaling, colour, and line thickness. The correct typesetting of these features requires a backend that supports it but even when this is not available Xy-pic tries to approximate what is requested such that at least the picture size is stable (and thus page breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply transformations for visual emphasis; be aware that precise rendering may depend on the driver/backend, but Xy-pic will approximate to preserve layout when full support is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: PostScript backend and literal PostScript inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Output can use PostScript for drawing (several \special formats are supported: dvips, Textures, and OzTeX - more are being added continuously). Notation for inclusion of literal PostScript is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PostScript backend for advanced drawing features; inclusion of literal PostScript is possible when driver supports it—check current supported backends.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF output support (xypdf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for Adobe PDF output is available from version 3.8 (thanks to support by Daniel Müllner and font conversion software by Scott Pakin). The xypdf package provides detailed user and TeXnical documentation of the PDF support for Xy-pic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install and consult the xypdf package and its documentation when targeting PDF output to ensure correct rendering and font handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation suite
rubrics_metrics.description: The official Xy-pic documentation consists of: Xy-pic User's Guide; Xy-pic Reference Manual; Xy-pic Complete Sources with TeXnical Commentary; the xypdf package documentation. In addition there are several tutorials and example collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the User's Guide for basic usage, the Reference Manual for syntax/semantics, the Complete Sources for internals, and xypdf docs for PDF specifics; use tutorials and CTAN examples for learning patterns and sample code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community support and announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Help and support on Xy-pic matters, as well as announcement of new versions, etc., is provided by the Xy-pic mailing list, graciously hosted by TUG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mailing list to ask usage questions, report issues, and learn about updates; contributions and tutorial suggestions are welcomed.
